## Summary

The sequence is **strongly supported as UbiE**, a bacterial ubiquinone/menaquinone-biosynthesis **C-methyltransferase**. It is 248 amino acids long and matches reviewed *Stenotrophomonas* and *Xanthomonas* UbiE proteins at about **77% identity**, covering 97.6% of the query. A UbiE-family domain (Pfam PF01209) was detected across residues 18–246.

UbiE is annotated to transfer a methyl group from **S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)** to quinol intermediates in quinone biosynthesis. The close homolog annotations include conversion of demethylmenaquinol to menaquinol, as well as methylation of a ubiquinone-pathway intermediate. This connects the protein to menaquinone biosynthesis and respiratory metabolism.

**Sequence-derived properties:** estimated mass 27.5 kDa; theoretical pI 9.30. These are computational estimates, not measurements. The exact organism, localization, and activity of this particular sequence were not experimentally established by the sequence analysis; the functional assignment is based on strong homology.
